title: Independent Ground
description: After this level you can operate independently in Tagalog. You see the focus system whole — actor, object, locative and benefactive voices laid out side by side — and choose the natural one based on what is definite and emphasized. You can say what you managed to do and what happened by accident, have things done for you with the causative, express feelings and reactions, and season your speech with the full particle toolkit: nga, pala, yata, sana, muna, tuloy. You can give and defend opinions politely, build complex sentences with relative clauses and embedded questions, report what other people said, handle a job interview or a phone call in the right register, and tell an extended story — including the trip where everything went wrong. You can also follow everyday conversations about news, weather and traffic, and you understand when and why Filipinos switch into Taglish.
canDo: I can describe the same event with actor, object, locative or benefactive focus and choose the one that fits what is definite and emphasized.
I can say what I managed to do, was able to do, or did by accident (nakapunta, nabasag, nakita).
I can arrange to have things done for me — get a haircut, have the car fixed — using the causative magpa-/pa--in/ipa-.
I can express feelings and reactions and describe things as tiring, funny, annoying or frightening.
I can use the particles nga, pala, yata, kaya, sana, muna and tuloy naturally and stack them in the right order.
I can give my opinion, agree and disagree politely, and hedge when I am not sure.
I can build conditional sentences, including unreal past conditions with sana, and link events with habang, hanggang and tuwing.
I can use relative clauses and embedded questions to build longer, connected sentences.
I can report what someone said or asked and retell a conversation.
I can handle a job interview, a formal phone call and scheduling in an appropriate register.
I can narrate an extended past story, including mishaps, with natural pacing words.
I can talk about news, traffic, weather and local events, and I understand when Taglish is and is not appropriate.
